questions.q: What problem do widgets solve, compared to hardcoding a value in a notebook cell?
options: They let you change an input, like a month string, without editing code in the notebook itself
They make a notebook run faster
They replace the need for a cluster entirely
They automatically fix any bugs in the surrounding code
questions.explain: This mirrors Foundations' Lesson 27 ETL capstone, which deliberately avoided one-off hardcoded values.

options: The widget's current value, always as a string regardless of the widget's type
A Python integer representing the month number
The default value only, never the current value someone typed in
A DataFrame containing every possible month
questions.explain: This is why you often see values cast or parsed further after reading them back.

questions.q: Why does a widget matter more for a job cluster than for interactive use?
options: A job cluster has no human present to edit code directly, so widget values must be supplied as parameters at run time instead
Widgets only function correctly on job clusters, never on all-purpose clusters
Job clusters cannot read any Python code at all without a widget
There's no real difference — widgets matter equally in both cases
questions.explain: This is exactly how one parameterized notebook becomes a reusable building block a schedule can run daily.

questions.q: What's the difference between a dropdown and a combobox widget?
options: A dropdown only allows a fixed list of choices; a combobox also accepts free-form typed input
They are functionally identical with no real difference
A combobox can only select one value, while a dropdown allows multiple
A dropdown is read differently than every other widget type
questions.explain: All widget types are still read back the same way, with dbutils.widgets.get().

questions.q: How does dbutils.widgets.text() create a usable input?
options: It takes a name, a default value, and a label, and adds an input box at the top of the notebook
It requires writing raw HTML to define the input box
It only works inside SQL cells, never Python cells
It automatically schedules a job to run using that input
questions.explain: Change the box and rerun the notebook, and the same logic runs against different input with no code edits.
